newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris stores tighten bomb security, shares drop.
newsitem.headline: Paris stores tighten bomb security, shares drop.

text.p: Paris department stores tightened security on Wednesday after a bomb blast the previous evening on a commuter train stirred investors' concern that sales might drop in the vital pre-Christmas season.

Shares in major stores fell on the Paris bourse because of worries that the train bombing, in which two people were killed and 79 were injured, might signal the start of a campaign of blasts that would keep shoppers out of city centres.
"We've reinforced security at each door," a spokesman for Galeries Lafayette on the boulevard Haussmann in central Paris said.

"That means more guards, systematic searches of bags, clients going through metal detectors," he said. The security matches that of 1995, when a wave of bombings by Algerian Islamic militants killed eight people and injured more than 160.

Other stores, including Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, Samaritaine, and local branches of Britain's Marks and Spencer Plc, also stepped up security as Paris ordered 1,800 troops to help police around France under the officially designated Vigipirate anti-terrorism plan.
"We've put the Vigipirate plan into place as much as possible in coordination with police headquarters," a spokesman for Printemps said.

Galeries Lafayette shares closed 3.2 percent weaker at 1,752 francs on fears of depressed sales. Pinault-Printemps-Redoute fell 0.73 percent to 2,050. Hotelier Accor ended 1.78 percent down at 663 francs.

Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre met representatives of department stores, shops, traders, cinema and theatre owners, hoteliers, cafe and discotheque owners on Wednesday to urge vigilance and urge them to step up checks.
Police similarly urged caution and regular security sweeps to check suspect packages and ensure emergency exits were clear.
